questions.q: Which of the following is **NOT** a memory-size unit?
questions.solution: **Mbps** = megabits per second — a data-transfer **speed**. TB, PB and GB are size units.

questions.q: The **RJ-45** socket on a computer is used for —
questions.solution: **RJ-45** is the Ethernet port — the tabbed socket that accepts the LAN cable.

questions.q: **PDF** (the extension .pdf) stands for —
questions.solution: **Portable Document Format** — a fixed-layout document that looks identical on every device, opened in readers like Adobe Reader or a browser.

questions.q: Which shortcut takes a web browser back to the previously visited page?
questions.solution: Alt+Left goes back and Alt+Right goes forward. Alt+Home opens the home page, and Ctrl+Left moves the cursor one word left in a text box.

questions.q: Select the phrasal verb that means *to refuse an offer or request*.
questions.solution: *Turn down* an offer = refuse it. *Turn up* = arrive; *turn out* = prove to be; *turn over* = flip, or hand over.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** Opening a savings account online now takes about fifteen minutes. **P:** Once the documents are checked, a short video call with a bank officer completes the process. **Q:** First, the applicant downloads the bank's app and enters her mobile number. **R:** She then uploads photos of her PAN card and Aadhaar card. **S:** An OTP sent to that number confirms her identity. **6.** The account number arrives by SMS the same day.
questions.solution: 'First' **Q** opens, and **S**'s 'that number' needs the number entered in **Q**. **P**'s 'the documents' are the cards uploaded in **R**, so **R****P** is a pair. Each step needs the one before it. **QSRP**.
questions.shortcut: Step dependencies: number -> OTP; upload -> documents checked.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

My friend **has gone** to Delhi yesterday to attend an interview.
questions.solution: The anchor *yesterday* demands the simple past → **went**. 'Had gone' removes the perfect but creates a sequence fault (no earlier event exists); 'has went' keeps the fault and adds a wrong form — both are two-fault traps.
questions.shortcut: fix the fault AND leave no new one behind.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

One who spends money wastefully
questions.solution: Wasteful spender = **spendthrift**. A miser saves excessively and hates spending — the opposite partner; a hoarder piles things up; a steward manages another's household.

questions.q: **Cheraw**, the bamboo dance in which dancers step in and out of clapping bamboo poles, belongs to —
questions.solution: **Cheraw** is the traditional bamboo dance of **Mizoram**, often performed at Chapchar Kut. Tripura's well-known dance is Hojagiri.
questions.shortcut: NE five: **Cheraw Mizo**, Hoja Tripura, Nong Khasi, Wang Garo, Bagu Bodo.

questions.q: The **Hoysala** capital **Dorasamudra** is today known as —
questions.solution: Dorasamudra is modern **Halebidu** (Karnataka); the Hoysaleswara temple stands there, and Belur's Chennakeshava temple is nearby.

questions.q: India stretches from about 68°7'E to 97°25'E. Roughly how much earlier does the Sun rise in the far east than in the far west?
questions.solution: Longitude gap = 97°25' - 68°7' = 29°18', about 29.3°. Time gap = 29.3 x 4 min, about 117 min - **nearly 2 hours**. This is why one Standard Meridian is needed.

questions.q: A judge of a **High Court** is appointed by —
questions.solution: **The President** appoints HC judges after consultation with the CJI and the state Governor (collegium recommendations since the Judges cases). Tenure runs to age **62**.

questions.q: A 20-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 3:1, and a 32-litre mixture has them in 5:3. If both are poured into one container, the ratio of milk to water is:
questions.shortcut: Add litres, not ratios — 3:1 and 5:3 cannot be summed directly.

questions.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a school is 4 : 5. If 100 more boys join the school, the ratio becomes 6 : 5. How many students were there in the school originally?
The average of 6 numbers is 15. If each number is multiplied by 3 and then increased by 5, the new average is:
questions.solution: New average $= 15 \times 3 + 5 = 50$.
questions.shortcut: Linear operations pass through the average: ×3 then +5 ⇒ 50.

questions.q: ₹780 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 3 : 4 : 6. What is A's share?
questions.solution:
Total parts = 13 → 1 part $= \frac{780}{13} = ₹60$.
A's share $= 3 \times 60 = ₹180$.

questions.q: **Rita's son is Amit. Amit's wife is Sneha.** How is **Sneha related to Rita**?
questions.solution: Sneha is the wife of Rita's son → **daughter-in-law**. (Sister-in-law would need Sneha to be a sibling of Rita or of Rita's spouse.)
questions.shortcut: Wife of my child = daughter-in-law; parent of my spouse = mother/father-in-law.

questions.q: Select the related letters: **DOT : TOD :: RAT : ?**
questions.solution: TOD is DOT **reversed**. Reversing RAT gives T-A-R → **TAR**.
questions.shortcut: Read the second cluster backwards; if it equals the first (or a constant shift of it), reverse the probe.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 144 144" width="144" height="144" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="12" y1="132" x2="132" y2="132"/><line x1="72" y1="12" x2="132" y2="132"/><line x1="12" y1="132" x2="72" y2="12"/><line x1="72" y1="12" x2="72" y2="132"/><line x1="12" y1="132" x2="102" y2="72"/><text x="72" y="7.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">A</text><text x="5" y="139.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">B</text><text x="139" y="139.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">C</text><text x="72" y="145.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">D</text><text x="110" y="75.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">E</text><text x="65" y="95.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">F</text></svg>
questions.solution: Use the letters on the figure (F is where the two inner lines cross). List triangles whose three sides are all drawn: ABC, ABD, ABE, ABF, ACD, AEF, BCE, BDF. Total = **8**.
questions.shortcut: Label corners and crossings; list triangles corner by corner.

questions.q:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

**15 ÷ 5 × 3 + 7 − 2 = 22**
questions.solution:
Right now the left side is 14, not 22. Try each option pair:

- 3 and 7: 15 ÷ 5 × 7 + 3 − 2 = 22 ✓
- 5 and 3: 15 ÷ 3 × 5 + 7 − 2 = 30 ✗
- 3 and 2: 15 ÷ 5 × 2 + 7 − 3 = 10 ✗
- 7 and 2: 15 ÷ 5 × 3 + 2 − 7 = 4 ✗

Only interchanging **3 and 7** balances the equation.
questions.shortcut: Sweep the option pairs in order; skip pairs that only swap the two sides of one ×.
